Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Below is how Redwood handles spend caps for hosted API customers (short version first, then details). Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Short answer:
- We do NOT silently bill unlimited overage. There are two behaviors depending on how the account is configured: a soft cap (recommended) that auto-throttles request rate and notifies admins, and a hard cutoff option that returns 429/402 once the hard limit is hit.
- For production-critical traffic we provide a documented emergency-override process that can provision a short-term credit or temporary increase while procurement completes a PO. This requires AE/finance approval.

Details:
1) Default behavior (soft cap):
   - When usage approaches the monthly budget threshold (we send alerts at 70%, 85%, 95%) the console will suggest batching & cache settings and temporarily reduce non-essential background jobs. At the threshold we apply progressive rate limiting per token (burst allowance + moving window) so live customer-facing requests continue but at a controlled level.
   - All requests still receive successful responses unless they exceed configured per-route priority. We log and emit events (billing.alert) for your SRE/observability.

2) Optional hard cutoff:
   - If you select hard cutoff in the account settings, once the cap is reached new requests will receive a 429 (Too Many Requests) with a billing reason header. No automatic post-facto billing for unlimited tokens occurs.

3) Emergency override / temporary credit:
   - Process: AE raises a MATP (Manual Adjustment & Temporary Provision) request -> finance validates -> CS or AE approves emergency credit. Typical SLA: 2–6 business hours depending on approvals.
   - We can provision temporary capacity for up to 72 hours or apply a one-time credit to smooth the procurement gap. We require a signed email approval from an authorized BrightLane finance contact to avoid abuse.

4) Invoicing & reconciliation:
   - Any temporary capacity used under emergency override is reconciled on the next invoice unless you provide a PO covering the delta. We can apply a credit if pre-arranged.

5) Recommended configuration for critical workloads:
   - Soft cap enabled + per-route priority for customer-facing endpoints + webhook alerts to your ops team + a runbook (I attached our policy).

Attached: Redwood_Overage_Policy_v2.pdf (summary + runbook).

If you want, I can loop in Marcus from Finance Ops to outline the approval matrix and timing.

Best,
Monica

Monica — short answers below. Copying in the MATP queue.

- MATP SLA: standard turnaround is 1–2 business days, but for accounts with enterprise support (BrightLane is on Enterprise Bronze) we can do 4–6 hours for amounts under $5k.
- Auto-provisioning: CS can enable temporary capacity immediately for up to $2k equivalent while finance processes approval for anything larger. That requires written authorization from a BrightLane finance approver (Sara or procurement).
- Exec signoff: any request > $25k requires VP-level signoff (sales manager + finance director).

Operational notes to include in reply:
- We'll set up a webhook that posts billing.alert events to BrightLane's slack channel and page on a runbook.
- For safety, configure priority routing so that customer-facing endpoints are exempt from non-essential background jobs in the soft-cap window.

Monica — you can confirm the specifics with Sara. I'll prepare a MATP form for immediate submission once they indicate the target amount.

Sara — thanks for the question and for the quick turnaround. Per Marcus above, here's the actionable path:

1) If you expect a short gap (<= $2k), reply to this thread with an authorized email from BrightLane finance and we will provision temporary capacity immediately (usually within 1 hour).
2) For larger one-off needs (<= $5k) we will open a MATP and aim for 4–6 hour SLA for Enterprise Bronze accounts.
3) Anything > $25k needs VP signoff and will follow our longer formal approval track.
